notes: Change is confined to scripts/e2e/api.py (+211) and scripts/e2e/README.md; no production code, no migration, no workflow — trivially revertible.

Every expectation in the new section was checked against the server: status/code pairs for each refusal (403 handoff_source_not_allowed before any dial, 400 handoff_claim_invalid, 404 handoff_claim_refused, 502 handoff_redirected, 415 handoff_unsupported_format, 502 handoff_source_unreachable) match refuseHandoff and the ordering in handoff.Fetch (allow list → ValidClaim → dial); 422 on a peer with a path / ftp scheme matches validateSettingValue → ParsePeers/strictOrigin; the unwrapped claim answer, RFC3339 expires_at, audit field names (targetId, metadata) and the import response shape (presentation/slides/warnings) all match handlers_handoff.go, model.AuditEntry and storeImportedSource.

The checks are real: the pptx handed back is opened as a zip and its byte count compared with the claim's promise; the fake peer records every request so 'not dialled' and 'dialled exactly once, without a credential' are asserted, not assumed; the audit trail is searched for the claim string. None of these would pass against a server lacking the feature.
Fabricated claim strings (e2e-good-<RUN>-xxxxxxxx etc.) are 24 chars in the [A-Za-z0-9_-] alphabet, so they pass ValidClaim and reach the peer as intended.

Cleanup runs in finally (peer thread shutdown, handoff.peers restored). Minor: if the key was never set it is restored as [] rather than removed; behaviourally identical for peersFrom, and the post-restore comparison tolerates it. peer_server.server_close() is not called, which only matters at process exit.

The 'server in a container' path degrades by printing and skipping the receiving half rather than failing, which is stated in the README and the script; the sending half (claim mint/redeem/audit) still runs unconditionally.

scripts/e2e/api.py:3244 the receive-success branch reuses deck_id which is still live at this point (last mutated at ~2913, never deleted) and was already exported as pptx at 2146, so the 201 claim path is reachable.
